manifest.summary: The Node adapter accepts spec-compliant FormData and Blob bodies, streams their bytes with computed headers, and retains the legacy form-data path.

items.title: Route FormData and Blob bodies through Node streams
items.before: The adapter recognized the package-specific form-data API and ordinary buffered or streamed bodies.
items.after: The adapter separately recognizes spec-compliant FormData, legacy form-data, and Blob bodies and supplies corresponding headers and streams.
items.statement: Body-type dispatch now selects multipart encoding or Blob reading before the existing buffered-body path.

items.title: Encode multipart parts and Blob bytes incrementally
items.before: No internal helpers serialized spec-compliant FormData or adapted Blob reading strategies.
items.after: New helpers encode multipart boundaries, part headers, content length, and Blob bytes as readable streams.
items.statement: Multipart output is assembled from each form entry and exposes computed content headers to the adapter.

items.title: Share FormData detection and platform construction
items.before: toFormData owned its spec-compliance predicate and imported the environment FormData class directly.
items.after: The predicate and boundary alphabet utilities are shared, while Node FormData construction uses the platform class.
items.statement: Form conversion and HTTP dispatch use the same spec-compliant FormData test.

items.title: Wire the test and browser environments
items.before: The tool configuration targeted ES2017 and did not include the FormData polyfill or browser mapping for the Node FormData class.
items.after: The configuration targets ES2018, provides a FormData test polyfill, and maps the Node-only class away in browser builds.
items.statement: Development and package metadata support the new runtime paths without vendoring their source.

items.title: Observe legacy FormData, spec FormData, and Blob uploads
items.before: The adapter test covered the package-specific form-data body.
items.after: The test distinguishes the legacy body and observes multipart fields, a file part, and a standalone Blob body.
items.statement: HTTP test servers parse or echo each body form and compare the received values.
